claim: For the Neumann–Kirchhoff path with edge lengths \((\varepsilon,a,b)\), with the short edge \(\varepsilon\) at an endpoint, and the Neumann–Kirchhoff three-arm star with the same lengths and \(\varepsilon\) attached at the hub, assume \(a,b>0\) and \(a\ne b\). For the first positive eigenstate, the diagonal geometric-phase response coefficient \(A_{11}=\varepsilon\,\partial_\varepsilon\langle\xi_1^2-\tfrac14\rangle\) satisfies \(A_{11}^{\mathrm{path}}=-\varepsilon/[3(a+b)]+O(\varepsilon^2)\) and \(A_{11}^{\mathrm{star}}=-\varepsilon\cos^2(\pi a/(a+b))/[3(a+b)]+O(\varepsilon^2)\) as \(\varepsilon\to0\); consequently the coefficients of the short-edge term \(\rho_1^2\nu_1^2\) in the leading quadratic adiabatic phase response have ratio \(\cos^2(\pi a/(a+b))\in(0,1)\).

correctness.rationale: The short-edge expectation equals the limiting vertex intensity times the exact integral -1/6. The path endpoint intensity tends to 2/(a+b); the star-hub intensity tends to 2 cos^2(pi a/(a+b))/(a+b). The path eigenfunction is explicit, and the star root near pi/(a+b) is simple by the tangent-sum identity and a≠b, so the asymptotic expansion can be differentiated.

value.rationale: The ratio gives a precise asymptotic diagnostic of the short edge’s attachment location: the same edge-length multiset yields a strictly reduced coefficient for the short-edge term in the leading quadratic phase expansion when the edge is attached at an interior point where the limiting excited eigenfunction has smaller intensity. This provides a concrete answer for one excited-state regime to the literature’s question of whether moving-graph geometric-phase data can reveal graph structure, without claiming complete graph identification.
